title: Earth Gravity Tunnel: Physics, Forces, and Lethal Effects of Drilling Through the Core
topic: Classical Mechanics, Newton's Shell Theorem, Geophysics & Orbital Dynamics
pedagogical_goal: Visually and quantitatively demonstrate the physics of drilling a straight borehole through the Earth and falling through it. Compare the idealized 42-minute Simple Harmonic Motion (Hooke's Law & Shell Theorem) against brutal real-world physical constraints: the Coriolis deflection that slams you into the tunnel wall, the 6,000°C core temperatures that vaporize matter, the 3.6 million atmosphere lithostatic pressure that crushes tunnel walls, and the exponential air column density that traps you in eternal weightless stagnation at the core.

fundamental_laws: Newton's Shell Theorem: Gravitational force inside a symmetric sphere depends only on enclosed mass: g(r) = G * M(r) / r²
Uniform Density Earth Model: g(r) = g₀ * (r / R_earth), producing Simple Harmonic Motion with period T = 2π * √(R_earth / g₀) ≈ 84.4 minutes (one-way transit = 42.2 minutes)
Realistic PREM (Preliminary Reference Earth Model): Core density (13 g/cm³) exceeds mantle (4.5 g/cm³), causing g(r) to peak at 10.7 m/s² at the core-mantle boundary (one-way transit = 38.2 minutes)
Conservation of Mechanical Energy (Vacuum): E_total = (1/2)mv² + U(r) = constant; Maximum velocity at core v_max = √(g₀ * R_earth) ≈ 7,900 m/s (28,440 km/h or Mach 23)
Coriolis Deflection: a_coriolis = -2 * (Ω_earth × v_fall); At non-polar latitudes, eastward surface velocity (up to 465 m/s) pushes falling bodies into the eastern wall
Atmospheric Drag & Hyper-Baric Density: If open to air, F_drag = (1/2) * ρ(r) * v² * C_d * A causes terminal velocity to collapse, permanently trapping the traveler at the center (r = 0)
Geothermal Gradient & Hydrostatic Lithostatic Pressure: P_core ≈ 360 GPa (3.6 million atmospheres), T_core ≈ 6,000°C

educational_cards.title: Why Does Transit Take 38–42 Minutes? (Newton's Shell Theorem)
educational_cards.content: By Newton's Shell Theorem, as you fall inside a planet, the entire spherical shell of matter above your current radius exerts zero net gravitational force on you—it pulls equally in all directions and cancels out! Only the smaller sphere of mass beneath you pulls you inward. In an idealized uniform Earth, this produces a restoring force strictly proportional to distance from the center (F = -kr), exactly like an ideal spring (Hooke's Law). The resulting Simple Harmonic Motion oscillation has a period of 84.4 minutes, meaning a one-way trip through Earth takes 42.2 minutes. With Earth's dense iron core (the realistic PREM model), gravity stays near 10 m/s² longer, speeding up the trip to 38.2 minutes!

educational_cards.title: Killer #1: The Coriolis Deflection (The Eastward Wall Smash)
educational_cards.content: Because Earth rotates from west to east, the ground at the equator moves eastward at 1,674 km/h (465 m/s). When you jump into an equatorial hole, you carry that 465 m/s eastward sideways momentum with you. But as you fall deeper toward the center, the surrounding rock closer to the axis moves much slower! By conservation of angular momentum, you travel eastward much faster than the shaft walls, slamming into the eastern wall at hundreds of kilometers per hour within minutes. The only way to fall straight through without hitting the wall is to drill precisely along Earth's rotational axis (North Pole to South Pole), or use active magnetic levitation tracks.

educational_cards.title: Killers #2 & #3: Hydrostatic Lithostatic Pressure & The 6,000°C Inferno
educational_cards.content: Even if you could somehow drill a hole, keeping it open is physically impossible with any known material. At depths beyond just 10–15 km, rocks become soft and behave like viscous plastic putty under immense pressure. At the core-mantle boundary (2,890 km) and core (6,371 km), lithostatic pressure reaches 3.6 million atmospheres (360 GPa) and temperatures hit 5,700°C–6,000°C (hotter than the surface of the Sun). Solid rock and liquid iron would instantaneously crush the tunnel shut like water flooding an open pipe in the ocean.

educational_cards.title: Killer #4: Air Resistance & Weightless Core Stagnation
educational_cards.content: What if you leave the tunnel open to the atmosphere? The weight of a 6,371 km tall column of air creates mind-boggling hyperbaric compression. At the core, atmospheric pressure would be so immense that air molecules would compress into a supercritical fluid denser than liquid water! Falling into this would not yield a hypersonic 28,000 km/h flight; instead, turbulent aerodynamic drag would quickly limit your speed to terminal velocity (~150–200 km/h) before air resistance slows you to a creeping crawl. You would oscillate a few times with decaying amplitude and end up permanently stuck, floating completely weightless at the center of the Earth, incinerated into ash.
